---
title: "Skill Gap Analysis"
subtitle: "Market Skill Demand and Career Readiness"
---

## Overview

This section connects our AI vs. non-AI career analysis to practical career readiness. Since our project focuses on how AI changes job security, industry demand, traditional career paths, and emerging job titles, the skill gap analysis looks at what job seekers need to strengthen in order to stay competitive.

Instead of treating AI as a separate career category, this section compares our team’s current skill profile with the skills that appeared most often in AI-related Lightcast job postings. The analysis uses the Lightcast findings from our exploratory analysis and a 1-5 team skill scale. No additional outside dataset is added in this section.

Because job postings do not directly measure layoffs or displacement, this section treats displacement as skill adaptation pressure. In other words, the main question is not only which jobs may disappear, but which skills help workers adjust as AI changes work across different fields.

## Team Skill Levels

The table below shows the current team skill profile using a 1-5 scale:

* 1 = Beginner
* 2 = Basic knowledge
* 3 = Intermediate
* 4 = Advanced
* 5 = Expert

```{python}
#| label: team-skill-dataframe
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

import pandas as pd
import plotly.express as px

skills_data = {
    "Team Member": ["Lutong", "Maria", "Sebastian", "Hye Won"],
    "Python": [3, 4, 3, 3],
    "SQL": [3, 3, 3, 3],
    "Machine Learning": [2, 4, 2, 2],
    "AI": [2, 3, 2, 3],
    "Data Analysis": [3, 4, 4, 3],
    "Data Visualization": [3, 4, 3, 3],
    "AWS": [1, 2, 2, 2],
    "Azure": [1, 1, 1, 1],
    "Communication": [4, 4, 4, 5]
}

df_skills = pd.DataFrame(skills_data).set_index("Team Member")
df_skills
```

## Skill Heatmap

The heatmap makes the team skill pattern easier to compare across members. Darker or higher values show stronger skills, while lower values show areas that need more development.

```{python}
#| label: team-skill-heatmap
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

fig = px.imshow(
    df_skills,
    text_auto=True,
    zmin=1,
    zmax=5,
    color_continuous_scale="RdYlGn",
    title="Team Skill Levels"
)

fig.update_layout(
    xaxis_title="Skill",
    yaxis_title="Team Member",
    height=500
)

fig.update_xaxes(tickangle=-30)

fig.show()
```

## Market Skill Demand

Based on our Lightcast job posting analysis, the most common skills in AI-related postings include SQL, Python, Data Analysis, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Data Science, Tableau, Statistics, Communication, AWS, Azure, Business Intelligence, Power BI, Data Visualization, and Data Modeling.

These results show that AI-related careers are not only about AI model development. Many AI-related roles also require data handling, programming, cloud tools, visualization, and communication skills.

To compare team readiness with the market, we converted the major in-demand skills into an industry expectation score from 1 to 5. This score is an interpretive rubric based on our EDA findings, not a new outside dataset. A higher score means the skill is more important for AI-related career readiness.

```{python}
#| label: industry-expectations
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

industry_expectations = pd.DataFrame({
    "Skill": [
        "Python",
        "SQL",
        "Machine Learning",
        "AI",
        "Data Analysis",
        "Data Visualization",
        "AWS",
        "Azure",
        "Communication"
    ],
    "Industry Expectation": [4, 4, 5, 5, 4, 4, 4, 3, 4]
})

team_average = (
    df_skills
    .mean()
    .round(2)
    .reset_index()
)

team_average.columns = ["Skill", "Team Average"]

gap_df = industry_expectations.merge(team_average, on="Skill")
gap_df["Gap"] = (gap_df["Industry Expectation"] - gap_df["Team Average"]).round(2)
gap_df = gap_df.sort_values("Gap", ascending=False).reset_index(drop=True)

gap_df
```

## Team Average vs. Industry Requirements

This chart compares the team average skill level with the expected skill level for AI-related roles. The largest gaps show where the team should focus first.

```{python}
#| label: skill-gap-chart
#| echo: true
#| message: false
#| warning: false

plot_df = gap_df.melt(
    id_vars="Skill",
    value_vars=["Team Average", "Industry Expectation"],
    var_name="Category",
    value_name="Score"
)

fig = px.bar(
    plot_df,
    x="Skill",
    y="Score",
    color="Category",
    barmode="group",
    title="Team Average vs. AI-Related Career Requirements",
    text="Score"
)

fig.update_layout(
    yaxis_title="Skill Level / Requirement Score",
    xaxis_title="Skill",
    yaxis_range=[0, 5.5],
    height=500
)

fig.update_xaxes(tickangle=-30)
fig.update_traces(textposition="outside")

fig.show()
```

## Skill Gap Interpretation

The largest gaps are in AI, machine learning, and cloud platforms. This matters because AI-related job postings increasingly require more than general business knowledge. Candidates are expected to understand technical tools, model-based workflows, and cloud-supported data systems.

From a job security perspective, this means that workers in many fields may face pressure if their work is highly routine or easy to automate. However, job seekers can improve their position by adding skills that are harder to replace, such as data analysis, AI literacy, cloud tools, business communication, and the ability to explain technical results.

For industries experiencing AI-driven growth, the skill gap points toward technical and analytics-heavy areas such as information technology, professional services, finance, manufacturing, healthcare, and education. For fields with higher displacement risk, the main issue is not that every job disappears, but that workers need to adapt their skill set as AI changes how tasks are performed.

AI-powered careers also differ from traditional roles because they combine domain knowledge with technical tools. For example, a traditional role in farming, retail, or mechanical engineering may still require industry expertise, but AI-powered versions of those jobs increasingly involve data, automation, predictive tools, dashboards, or AI-supported decision-making.

Emerging job titles also reflect this shift. Roles such as AI Analyst, Machine Learning Engineer, Data Scientist, MLOps Engineer, Business Intelligence Analyst, and AI Product Analyst show that job seekers need a mix of technical, analytical, and communication skills.

## Improvement Plan

The table below translates the main gaps into a practical improvement plan.

| Priority Area                | Why It Matters                                                                                                 | Recommended Action                                                                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| AI and Machine Learning      | AI-related careers increasingly require model-based thinking and machine learning literacy.                    | Practice classification, regression, clustering, and model interpretation projects.                                        |
| Cloud Platforms              | Cloud tools such as AWS and Azure appear in AI-related job postings and support modern data workflows.         | Continue AWS labs and learn basic cloud deployment and data storage workflows.                                             |
| Data and Dashboard Reporting | AI-related roles still require clear reporting, visualization, and business communication.                     | Build Tableau, Power BI, or Plotly dashboards using job market or business datasets.                                       |
| Industry Translation         | Traditional fields are not separate from AI; many roles now require both domain knowledge and technical tools. | Connect technical findings to specific industries such as healthcare, finance, manufacturing, retail, and farming.         |
| Emerging AI Job Titles       | New AI-related job titles show that the job market is changing and candidates need updated skill combinations. | Track AI Analyst, Machine Learning Engineer, Data Scientist, MLOps, and BI Analyst postings to understand required skills. |

## Connection to the Four Research Questions

| Research Focus                                 | Skill Gap Connection                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| AI and job security across fields              | Job security depends on whether workers can add data, AI, cloud, and communication skills to their existing field knowledge.                                                                  |
| AI-driven job growth vs. displacement pressure | AI-related demand is more visible in technical, analytical, financial, healthcare, manufacturing, and service-related industries, while routine task areas face stronger adaptation pressure. |
| AI-powered careers vs. traditional roles       | AI-powered careers require traditional domain knowledge plus technical tools such as Python, SQL, machine learning, dashboards, and cloud platforms.                                          |
| Emerging job titles                            | Titles such as AI Analyst, Machine Learning Engineer, Data Scientist, MLOps Engineer, and AI Product Analyst show that job seekers need updated skill combinations.                           |

Overall, the skill gap analysis shows that our team already has a foundation in data analysis, SQL, visualization, and communication. The main improvement areas are AI, machine learning, and cloud platforms. Strengthening these skills would help connect our current business analytics background to AI-related career opportunities.
